source.title: Costa-Araújo et al. (2024) — A dataset of new occurrence records of primates from the arc of deforestation, Brazil
source.version: Primate Biology 11:1–11; version of record published 2024-01-22.
source.attribution: Costa-Araújo R, Canale GR, de Melo FR, da Silva RR, da Silva IB, de Alencar RM, da Silva LF, Jerusalinsky L, de Azevedo RB, Santos Júnior EM, Mourthé I, Ruz EJH, Silva-Jr. JdSe, Roos C, Farias IP, and Hrbek T. (2024). A dataset of new occurrence records of primates from the arc of deforestation, Brazil. Primate Biology 11:1–11. https://doi.org/10.5194/pb-11-1-2024. Findings paraphrased.
source.scope: Ten field expeditions in southern Amazonia, Brazil, during 2015–2018 produced 192 occurrence records for 22 species and subspecies across 56 localities. The article discusses range records and taxonomic hypotheses for selected taxa; this batch reuses only its bounded occurrence and range statements.
source.locator: Publisher article: Methods, 2015–2018 expeditions and identification methods; Results and discussion, paragraphs on the eight range-clarification taxa, the Juruena and Teles Pires records, titi-monkey range delimitation, and Saimiri collinsi; Conclusions on remaining taxonomy and field-data gaps.

supplement.title: Costa-Araújo et al. (2024) — Supplement: Dataset of 192 new occurrence records of primates from the arc of deforestation, Brazil
supplement.version: Eight-page publisher supplement to Primate Biology 11:1–11; published 2024.
supplement.scope: Supplementary locality table for 192 records across 22 species and subspecies. These profiles paraphrase broad municipality/state coverage only; they do not reproduce coordinates, the table, or graphics.

identitySource.title: Catalogue of Life COL26.8 / ChecklistBank dataset 316115
identitySource.scope: Taxonomic identity only: accepted species usage, authorship, rank, status, and parent classification through Primates usage 3W7. It does not support biological claims.

targets.scope: The article discusses Alouatta discolor in relation to a historical locality record and a possible contact zone with the paper's Alouatta puruensis. COL26.8 does not return Alouatta puruensis as an accepted primate species; that source name is retained as a dated label and is not mapped to another accepted species here.
targets.claim: The authors describe a prior report of sympatry between A. discolor and the paper's A. puruensis in the Juruena–Teles Pires interfluve and suggest that nearby records may indicate a contact or hybridization zone. Hybridization and bidirectional gene flow remain hypotheses, not confirmed outcomes.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraphs beginning 'Based on current knowledge...' and 'One of our records of Alouatta puruensis...'; Conclusions on additional records and genetic samples needed.

targets.scope: Two occurrence records from the right bank of the middle Teles Pires River in southern Amazonia; one overlaps a published Ateles marginatus record.
targets.claim: Two black-pelaged spider monkeys lacking the white forehead and cheek hairs characteristic of A. marginatus were identified as A. chamek on the right bank of the middle Teles Pires, within the mapped range of A. marginatus; one record overlaps an A. marginatus locality. The authors propose possible river-crossing dispersal and gene flow, which they say needs further field and genetic evidence.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'Two of our records of Ateles chamek...'; Conclusions on refining taxonomy, extent of occurrence, and testing gene flow.

targets.scope: One A. marginatus locality overlaps a new Ateles chamek record in the middle Teles Pires region; evidence concerns the local range boundary.
targets.claim: The paper reports one A. chamek occurrence overlapping an A. marginatus locality on the right bank of the middle Teles Pires. The authors suggest that river islands could permit movement and gene flow between the populations, but explicitly call for more records and genetic samples to test this proposal.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'Two of our records of Ateles chamek...'; Conclusions on additional records, specimens, and genetic samples.

targets.scope: A proposed regional range delimitation from occurrence records in southern Amazonia, considered alongside ranges assigned to Plecturocebus grovesi and P. vieirai.
targets.claim: The authors propose a revised regional range for P. moloch using their records and excluding areas assigned to P. grovesi and P. vieirai. They also state that the type locality, two historical synonyms, and titi taxonomy in the Jamanxim–Teles Pires interfluve still need clarification.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'We propose a new delimitation...'; Conclusions on unresolved taxonomy and need for additional field data.

targets.scope: A local occurrence of Plecturocebus baptista within the area then attributed to P. hoffmannsi, in a region with limited taxonomic and distribution evidence.
targets.claim: The study records P. baptista within the range attributed to P. hoffmannsi and notes earlier records in the same area. It raises clinal phenotype variation as a possible explanation, while stating that molecular phylogenetic analyses are lacking and taxonomy remains unresolved.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'We found a group of P. baptista...'; Conclusions on the need to clarify taxonomy, distribution, and evolutionary history.

targets.scope: A local occurrence record within the area attributed by the article to Plecturocebus hoffmannsi; the paper discusses possible clinal variation but does not test species boundaries genetically.
targets.claim: The authors report P. baptista within the range assigned to P. hoffmannsi. Because the two forms are poorly studied, have not been evaluated together with molecular phylogenetic analyses, and lack an obvious geographic barrier to gene flow, the paper raises a single-species clinal-variation interpretation as a hypothesis rather than a taxonomic result.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'We found a group of P. baptista...'; Conclusions on additional taxonomy and distribution work.

targets.scope: Occurrence records from the Jamanxim, upper Tapajós, and lower Teles Pires river region in southern Amazonia, based on field expeditions during 2015–2018.
targets.claim: The authors recorded S. collinsi on the left bank of the Jamanxim River and on the right bank of the upper Tapajós and lower Teles Pires rivers. They estimated that these points extend the then-known range about 600 km west; this is a regional range inference, not a population census or current full-range survey.
targets.locator: Results and discussion, paragraph beginning 'Finally, we recorded Saimiri collinsi...'; Methods on expedition dates and occurrence-identification approach.

targets.scope: Two observation records in Altamira and Anapu, Pará, in the supplementary occurrence table.
targets.claim: The supplement lists two observation records of Alouatta belzebul in Pará, at Altamira and Anapu. These are local records from the 2015–2018 field program, not a range-wide survey or abundance estimate.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Alouatta belzebul rows on page 1.

targets.sourceTaxonomyMapping: COL26.8 accepted subspecies 5FP8B is classified under accepted species Aotus azarae F6F4.
targets.scope: One observation in Altamira, Pará, listed under the source subspecies name Aotus azarae infulatus.
targets.claim: The supplement records one observation in Altamira, Pará, under A. azarae infulatus. COL26.8 accepts that subspecies under A. azarae; this page is attached to the current accepted species and keeps the study's subspecies label visible.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Aotus azarae infulatus row on page 1; COL26.8 accepted subspecies usage 5FP8B and parent species F6F4.

targets.scope: Two observation records at Apuí, Amazonas, in the supplementary occurrence table.
targets.claim: The supplement lists two Cebus unicolor observations from Apuí in Amazonas during the multi-expedition field program. These records locate the species in the sampled municipality but do not establish its complete distribution or population status.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Cebus unicolor rows on page 2.

targets.scope: Occurrence records in Pará, Amazonas, Mato Grosso, and Rondônia, including observation and vocalization records.
targets.claim: The supplementary table places red-nosed bearded sakis at sampled localities in four Brazilian states: Pará, Amazonas, Mato Grosso, and Rondônia. The table includes both observation and vocalization records; it is a field-record dataset, not a census or complete range assessment.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Chiropotes albinasus rows on pages 2–3.

targets.sourceTaxonomyMapping: COL26.8 records source name 5J8RN as a synonym under accepted species Lagothrix lagothricha 6NTWV; accepted subspecies Lagothrix lagothricha cana is 5J8RQ.
targets.scope: Locality records in Amazonas and Rondônia under the source name Lagothrix cana cana, which COL26.8 treats as a synonym under accepted species L. lagothricha.
targets.claim: The supplement records the woolly monkey using the name L. cana cana at sampled municipalities in Amazonas and Rondônia. COL26.8 places that source name under accepted L. lagothricha; the records are retained as a dated taxonomic usage and local occurrence set, not evidence for a complete species range.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Lagothrix cana cana rows on pages 3–4; COL26.8 synonym usage 5J8RN and accepted species 6NTWV.

targets.sourceTaxonomyMapping: COL26.8 accepted subspecies 7JWMG is classified under accepted species Leontocebus weddelli 3T6RQ.
targets.scope: Two observation records in Candeias do Jamari and Itapuã do Oeste, Rondônia, listed under the accepted subspecies Leontocebus weddelli weddelli.
targets.claim: The supplement lists two observations under L. weddelli weddelli in Rondônia, at Candeias do Jamari and Itapuã do Oeste. COL26.8 accepts that subspecies under L. weddelli; these records do not survey the species' full range.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Leontocebus weddelli weddelli rows on page 3; COL26.8 accepted subspecies 7JWMG and parent species 3T6RQ.

targets.scope: Local occurrence records in Apuí and Humaitá, Amazonas, and Cotriguaçu, Mato Grosso.
targets.claim: The supplement lists Pithecia mittermeieri observations from Apuí and Humaitá in Amazonas and Cotriguaçu in Mato Grosso. These municipalities describe sampled occurrences in one survey program, not a complete distribution or abundance estimate.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Pithecia mittermeieri rows on pages 3–4.

targets.authorship: (M. van Roosmalen, T. van Roosmalen & Mittermeier, 2002)
targets.scope: Locality records in Humaitá, Amazonas, and Ji-Paraná, Rondônia.
targets.claim: The supplementary table records Prince Bernhard's titi at Humaitá in Amazonas and Ji-Paraná in Rondônia. These locations are points from the 2015–2018 field program, not a full range map or population assessment.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Plecturocebus bernhardi rows on pages 4–5.

targets.scope: Three observation records at Candeias do Jamari and Itapuã do Oeste, Rondônia.
targets.claim: Three P. brunneus observations in the supplement come from two Rondônia municipalities, Candeias do Jamari and Itapuã do Oeste. This is a local record set, not a complete distribution or population survey.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Plecturocebus brunneus rows on page 5.

targets.scope: Occurrence records at Apuí, Amazonas, and Cotriguaçu, Mato Grosso.
targets.claim: The supplement records ashy titis in Apuí, Amazonas, and Cotriguaçu, Mato Grosso, including observation and vocalization records. These are surveyed localities, not a full range inventory.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Plecturocebus cinerascens rows on page 5.

targets.authorship: Boubli, Byrne, M. N. F. Silva, Silva-Júnior, Costa-Araújo, Bertuol, Gonçalves, Melo, Rylands, et al., 2019
targets.scope: Two occurrence records at Paranaíta and Nova Bandeirantes, Mato Grosso.
targets.claim: The supplementary table lists a Paranaíta observation and a Nova Bandeirantes vocalization record for Groves' titi, both in Mato Grosso. The record types and municipalities are local evidence and do not establish a complete range or population size.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Plecturocebus grovesi rows on page 5.

targets.scope: Occurrence records at Apuí and Novo Aripuanã, Amazonas.
targets.claim: Milton's titis in the supplement are recorded at Apuí and Novo Aripuanã in Amazonas. The dataset provides local occurrence points from the survey period, not a complete distribution or status assessment.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Plecturocebus miltoni rows on pages 5–6.

targets.scope: Occurrence records in Amazonas, Rondônia, and Mato Grosso, including observation and vocalization records.
targets.claim: The supplement places bare-eared squirrel monkeys at sampled localities in Amazonas, Rondônia, and Mato Grosso, with both observation and vocalization record types. These field records do not constitute a complete species-range survey or abundance estimate.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Saimiri ustus rows on pages 6–7.

targets.sourceTaxonomyMapping: COL26.8 accepted subspecies 7L2JH is classified under accepted species Sapajus apella 6XJVY.
targets.scope: Numerous locality records across Pará, Amazonas, Rondônia, and Mato Grosso under the accepted source subspecies name Sapajus apella apella.
targets.claim: The supplement lists S. apella apella records from multiple municipalities in Pará, Amazonas, Rondônia, and Mato Grosso. COL26.8 accepts that subspecies under S. apella; the table represents survey occurrences, not a census or complete range assessment.
targets.locator: Supplement, locality table, Sapajus apella apella rows on pages 6–8; COL26.8 accepted subspecies 7L2JH and parent species 6XJVY.

gaps: These are regional occurrence and taxonomy-context guides, not complete species accounts, abundance estimates, or conservation assessments.
The source uses some species and subspecies concepts that differ from current COL26.8; Alouatta puruensis was not silently cross-mapped because an accepted COL26.8 primate usage was not verified.
The authors identify additional field records, specimens, and genetic samples as necessary for testing range boundaries, hybridization, and titi-monkey taxonomy.
The profiles are source-linked and not externally expert-reviewed; no species dossier is added.
